theory.title: Food, quantities and ordering meals
theory.explanation: Use countable nouns for things you can count (an apple, two eggs) and uncountable nouns for substances or general food (rice, milk, bread). Use how many with plural countable nouns and how much with uncountable nouns. Use some in positive sentences and polite offers or requests; use any in most questions and negatives. Use a few and a little for small quantities. In cafés and restaurants, I'd like and Could I have are polite ways to order.
theory.tip: Remember: many apples but much water; a few eggs but a little milk. Say I'd like + noun, not I'd like to + noun.

content.passage: On Saturday, Mia goes to the market with her dad. They need some apples, a few tomatoes, a bottle of milk and a little cheese. Mia asks, “How many apples do we need?” Her dad says, “Six, please.” At lunchtime, they visit a small café. Mia looks at the menu and says, “I'd like a chicken sandwich and some water, please.” Her dad orders soup and tea. The waiter asks if they would like anything else. They say no, and later ask for the bill. The food is delicious, and they decide to come back next week.

content.audioTranscript: Hello. Are you ready to order? Yes, please. I'd like a tomato soup and a cheese sandwich. Would you like something to drink? Could I have a glass of water, please? Of course. And for you? I'd like the chicken salad and an orange juice. How many people are eating today? Just two. Anything else? No, thank you. Could we have the bill later, please? Certainly.
